docs.title: AI Agents and Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard automates invoice processing through a multi-agent AI pipeline. Five specialized agents operate in sequence across seven pipeline stages, each performing a distinct function: validation, tax identification, tax calculation, risk assessment, and report generation.

Agent operational status is tracked in real time in the AgentStatus entity and displayed in the dashboard's AI Agent Status panel. If an agent encounters an error, the pipeline stage status updates immediately, giving finance operators instant visibility without polling.

docs.title: AI Agents
docs.text:
The following agents are registered in the AgentStatus entity and appear in the Agent Status panel:

AI Agent Roles

Agent Role Output Invoice Validator Checks invoice structure, required fields, and vendor data integrity `validationErrors` field on the Invoices entity; AI validation score Tax Selector Identifies the correct tax type \(for example, VAT, GST\) based on vendor jurisdiction `tax` and `vatRate` fields on the Invoices entity Tax Calculator Computes tax amount and net amount from gross amount and identified tax rate `taxAmount` and `netAmount` fields on the Invoices entity Risk and Anomaly Scorer Assigns a risk level and overall compliance score; flags anomalies for review `riskLevel`, `score`, `complianceScore`, and Alerts entity records Report Generator Produces the AI verdict summary and populates KPI and trend data `aiVerdict` field; KPIMetrics and MonthlyTrends entity updates

docs.title: Seven-Stage Processing Pipeline
docs.text:
Each invoice moves through seven sequential stages. The PipelineStages entity stores the definition and current status of each stage. The dashboard renders these stages with visual flow connectors and status icons.

Invoice Processing Pipeline Stages

Stage Name Agent Responsible Output 1 Invoice Ingestion \- Invoice record created in the `Invoices` entity with status `Pending` 2 Structure Validation Invoice Validator Validation errors written; score assigned 3 Tax Identification Tax Selector Tax type and VAT rate populated 4 Tax Calculation Tax Calculator Tax amount and net amount computed 5 Risk and Anomaly Scoring Risk and Anomaly Scorer Risk level, compliance score, and alert records written 6 Report Generation Report Generator AI verdict written; KPI metrics and monthly trend updated 7 Review and Disposition Finance user Invoice approved or rejected via the detail dialog; status updated

docs.title: Agent Status Monitoring
docs.text:
The AgentStatus entity tracks the runtime state of each agent. Each record has a status field that the dashboard reads and displays in the AI Agent Status panel. The status values used in the mock data are:

  • Active — the agent is running and processing invoices
  • Idle — the agent is available but has no current work
  • Error — the agent encountered a fault; check details for the error message

The dashboard refreshes agent status automatically. If you integrate a real AI agent backend, update the AgentStatus records via OData PATCH or through a custom CAP action to reflect actual runtime state.

docs.title: Tip:
docs.text: In a production deployment, consider exposing a CAP action — for example, triggerPipelineRun — that triggers the agent pipeline for a batch of invoices and writes status updates asynchronously. This pattern keeps the UI decoupled from agent execution latency.

docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard uses seven Core Data Services (CDS) entities defined in db/schema.cds. Each entity maps directly to an OData V4 entity set exposed by the FinanceService, and all entities are seeded with mock data in CSV files under db/data/ for local development.

The data model is intentionally flat to maximize OData query performance and simplify frontend binding. Relationships between entities are navigated at the service level through OData query parameters.

docs.title: Entity Definitions
docs.text: The CDS schema defines the following entities in the db namespace:

docs.title: Invoices
docs.text:
The Invoices entity is the central business object. It captures the full lifecycle of a single invoice, from the raw vendor amount through tax calculation, AI validation, compliance scoring, and final disposition.

Invoice Entity Fields

Field Type Description `ID` String \(key\) Unique invoice identifier `vendor` String Vendor or supplier name `amount` Decimal\(15, 2\) Gross invoice amount `tax` String Tax type identifier \(for example, VAT, GST\) `taxAmount` Decimal\(15, 2\) Calculated tax amount `score` Integer AI-assigned validation score \(0–100\) `status` String Processing status \(for example, Pending, Approved, Rejected\) `date` Date Invoice date `complianceScore` Integer Compliance assessment score \(0–100\) `riskLevel` String Risk classification \(High, Medium, Low\) `aiVerdict` String AI agent decision summary `details` String Human-readable invoice summary `referenceNumber` String External reference or purchase order number `currency` String ISO 4217 currency code `validationErrors` String Comma-separated list of AI validation errors `vatRate` String Applicable VAT rate as a percentage string `netAmount` Decimal\(15, 2\) Net amount before tax

docs.title: Supporting Entities
docs.text:
The following entities provide supporting reference data for the dashboard:

Supporting Entities

Entity Purpose Key Fields `ComplianceScores` Category-wise compliance metrics shown as progress bars `category`, `percentage`, `color`, `description` `Alerts` Risk and anomaly alerts with severity classification `title`, `severity`, `status`, `details`, `color` `AgentStatus` Real-time operational status of each AI agent `name`, `subtitle`, `status`, `icon` `PipelineStages` Definition and current status of each processing pipeline stage `title`, `subtitle`, `status`, `order` `KPIMetrics` Key performance indicator values with trend direction `title`, `value`, `trend`, `trendDir` `MonthlyTrends` Historical monthly invoice volume for bar chart visualization `month`, `value`, `year`

docs.title: Mock Data
docs.text:
All entities are seeded with CSV files in db/data/. The file naming convention is db-EntityName.csv. These files are loaded automatically when you run the application in development mode using npm run watch.

The mock data includes sample invoices with varied compliance scores and risk levels, so you can test all dashboard states without connecting to a real data source.

docs.title: Tip:
docs.text: To add your own test invoices, edit db/data/db-Invoices.csv directly and restart the development server. The SAP CAP runtime reloads CSV data on restart.

docs.title: CDS Source
docs.text:
The complete CDS data model is in db/schema.cds. The full namespace is db, and all entities are referenced in the service layer as db.EntityName.

namespace db;

entity Invoices {
    key ID               : String;
        vendor           : String;
        amount           : Decimal(15, 2);
        tax              : String;
        taxAmount        : Decimal(15, 2);
        score            : Integer;
        status           : String;
        date             : Date;
        complianceScore  : Integer;
        riskLevel        : String;
        aiVerdict        : String;
        details          : String;
        referenceNumber  : String;
        currency         : String;
        validationErrors : String;
        vatRate          : String;
        netAmount        : Decimal(15, 2);
}

For guidance on OData support in SAP CAP, see Maintaining OData Services in SAP HANA Cloud .

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard runs locally for development using SQLite and the SAP CAP watch mode server. For production, it deploys to SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) via Cloud Foundry using a Multi-Target Application (MTA) archive. An alternative deployment path to SAP HANA is also available for organizations already using SAP HANA Platform.

This guide covers both the local development setup and the full BTP deployment procedure.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you start, ensure the following are available on your machine:

  • Node.js version 18 or higher
  • npm version 8 or higher
  • SAP CDS CLI, installed globally: npm install -g @sap/cds-dk
  • For BTP deployment: Cloud Foundry CLI with the MultiApps plugin installed
  • For BTP deployment: An active SAP BTP subaccount with a Cloud Foundry space

docs.title: Local Development Setup
docs.text:
To run the application locally:

  1. Clone or copy the project to your local machine.

  2. Install all Node.js dependencies:

    npm install

  3. Start the development server with file watching enabled:

    npm run watch

  4. Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:4004.

  5. Choose the finance-dashboard tile to open the application.

The npm run watch command starts the SAP CAP server in development mode. It loads the SQLite in-memory database, seeds it with CSV mock data from db/data/, and serves both the OData service and the SAP UI5 frontend from the same port.

Available Development Commands

Command Description `npm start` Run in production mode \(no file watching\) `npm run watch` Run in development mode with automatic reload on file changes `npm run build` Build the project for production packaging `npm run serve` Serve with in-memory SQLite database `npm run deploy` Deploy the database schema to SAP HANA

docs.title: Note:
docs.text: In development mode, all data is held in memory and resets on each server restart. To persist changes across restarts, configure a file-based SQLite database or switch to SAP HANA.

docs.title: SAP BTP Cloud Foundry Deployment
docs.text:
The application is packaged as a Multi-Target Application using mta.yaml. The MTA format bundles the SAP CAP service module and the SAP UI5 frontend module into a single deployable archive.

For reference, see Deploy the Migrated SAP CAP Application to SAP BTP .

To deploy to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry:

  1. Log in to your Cloud Foundry organization and target your deployment space:

    cf login -a <api-endpoint>
cf target -o <org> -s <space>

  2. Build the MTA archive using the MTA Build Tool:

    mbt build

    This creates a .mtar file under mta_archives/.

  3. Deploy the archive to Cloud Foundry:

    cf deploy mta_archives/finance-dashboard_1.0.0.mtar

  4. Monitor deployment progress in the terminal. After a successful deployment, the application URL is printed in the output.

For guidance on the mta.yaml descriptor format, see Maintaining the Multitarget Application Development and Deployment Descriptors .

docs.title: SAP HANA Deployment
docs.text:
If your organization uses SAP HANA Platform directly (without Cloud Foundry MTA), you can deploy the CAP database schema with a single CDS command:

cds deploy --to hana

This command generates the HDI (HANA Deployment Infrastructure) artifacts and pushes the schema to the connected SAP HANA instance. Ensure that the HANA connection details are configured in your ~/.cdsrc.json or as environment variables before running this command.

docs.title: Caution:
docs.text: Running cds deploy --to hana on an existing production database will apply schema migrations. Review the generated HDI artifacts before deploying to a production environment to avoid unintended data loss.

docs.title: Verifying the Deployment
docs.text:
After starting the server — locally or on BTP — you can verify that the OData service is running by navigating to the service document:

http://<host>:4004/finance/

To test individual entity sets, navigate to:

http://<host>:4004/finance/Invoices

A JSON response containing invoice records confirms that the service and database connection are working correctly.

docs.title: OData Service Layer
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard exposes all business data through a single OData V4 service called FinanceService. The service is defined in srv/service.cds using CDS projections and implemented in srv/service.js with custom event handlers for logging, error handling, and post-processing.

In development mode, the service is available at http://localhost:4004/finance/. In production on SAP BTP, the path is resolved through the Cloud Foundry route configured in mta.yaml.

docs.title: Service Definition
docs.text:
The FinanceService is defined as a set of CDS projections on the underlying database entities. This approach means you can evolve the data model and service independently — projection-level annotations or filters can be applied without changing the core schema.

using db from '../db/schema';

service FinanceService {
    entity Invoices         as projection on db.Invoices;
    entity ComplianceScores as projection on db.ComplianceScores;
    entity Alerts           as projection on db.Alerts;
    entity AgentStatus      as projection on db.AgentStatus;
    entity PipelineStages   as projection on db.PipelineStages;
    entity KPIMetrics       as projection on db.KPIMetrics;
    entity MonthlyTrends    as projection on db.MonthlyTrends;
}

For a full reference on OData V4 services in SAP CAP, see Maintaining OData Services in SAP HANA Cloud .

docs.title: Available Endpoints
docs.text:
When the application is running, the following OData entity set endpoints are available under the /finance/ path:

OData V4 Entity Set Endpoints

Endpoint Entity Set Description `/finance/Invoices` Invoices Invoice records with AI scores, risk levels, and compliance data `/finance/ComplianceScores` ComplianceScores Category-wise compliance metric percentages `/finance/Alerts` Alerts Risk and anomaly alerts with severity and status `/finance/AgentStatus` AgentStatus Operational status of each AI processing agent `/finance/PipelineStages` PipelineStages Processing pipeline stage definitions and current status `/finance/KPIMetrics` KPIMetrics Key performance indicator values with trend direction `/finance/MonthlyTrends` MonthlyTrends Historical monthly invoice volume data for charting

To browse the service metadata, navigate to http://localhost:4004/finance/$metadata during development.

docs.title: Service Implementation
docs.text: The srv/service.js file adds custom event handlers on top of the default CAP auto-CRUD behavior. The implementation covers three concerns: pre-read logging, custom KPI read handling, and global error and post-read telemetry.

docs.title: KPIMetrics Custom Handler
docs.text:
The KPIMetrics entity uses a custom READ handler instead of relying solely on the CAP generic handler. This pattern is used when you need to intercept or transform data before it reaches the client.

srv.on('READ', 'KPIMetrics', async (req) => {
    const result = await req.query;
    return result;
});

docs.title: Global Error Handler
docs.text:
The service registers a global error handler that logs the entity name and stack trace for any runtime error:

srv.on('error', (err, req) => {
    console.error('GLOBAL ERROR:', err.message);
    console.error('   Entity:', req.target?.name);
    console.error('   Stack:', err.stack);
});

docs.title: Post-Read Logging
docs.text:
An after('READ', '*') hook runs after every successful read across all entities. It logs the entity name and the record count returned, which is useful for performance diagnostics:

srv.after('READ', '*', (data, req) => {
    const entityName = req.target.name;
    const count = Array.isArray(data) ? data.length : 1;
    console.log(`Returned ${count} records for ${entityName}`);
    return data;
});

docs.title: Note:
docs.text: The global after('READ', '*') hook introduces a small overhead on every read operation. In high-throughput production environments, consider replacing it with entity-specific hooks on only the entities that require monitoring.

docs.title: OData Query Examples
docs.text:
You can use standard OData V4 query parameters to filter and sort results during development. The following examples demonstrate typical queries:

Filter high-risk invoices:

/finance/Invoices?$filter=riskLevel eq 'High'

Sort invoices by compliance score descending:

/finance/Invoices?$orderby=complianceScore desc

Select specific fields from KPI metrics:

/finance/KPIMetrics?$select=title,value,trendDir

docs.title: Finance Intelligence Dashboard Overview
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard is an enterprise-grade application built with SAP UI5 and the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (CAP). It provides real-time visibility into invoice processing workflows, compliance metrics, risk alerts, and AI-driven automation across a 7-stage processing pipeline.

This documentation covers the system architecture, key capabilities, and how the frontend and backend layers interact to deliver intelligent financial operations on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP).

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard combines the declarative power of SAP CAP with the rich UI capabilities of SAP UI5 to deliver a complete, full-stack finance automation solution. At its core, the application processes invoices through an AI-powered pipeline that validates, calculates taxes, scores risk, and generates reports automatically — without manual intervention.

The application is designed for finance teams who need a single consolidated view across invoice status, compliance health, and risk exposure. It surfaces AI agent activity in real time, making it easy to identify bottlenecks, flag anomalies, and take corrective action without leaving the dashboard.

For more information about SAP Cloud Application Programming Model, see Working with the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model .

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
The application follows a three-tier architecture: an SAP UI5 frontend, an SAP CAP service layer, and a database tier backed by SQLite in development and SAP HANA in production. All tiers are packaged together as a Multi-Target Application (MTA) for deployment to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry.

System Components

Component Role Technology Finance Dashboard UI Frontend application with XML views, fragments, and controllers SAP UI5 \(MVC, XML views\) FinanceService OData V4 service exposing all business entities SAP CAP \(CDS, Node.js\) Database Layer Stores invoices, compliance scores, alerts, and trend data SQLite \(development\), SAP HANA \(production\) AI Agent Framework Validates, calculates tax, scores risk, and generates reports on invoices Node.js microservices MTA Deployment Packages and deploys all modules to SAP BTP Cloud Foundry MTA \(mta.yaml\), Cloud Foundry CLI 
graph TB
  User[Finance User] --> UI[SAP UI5 Dashboard]
  UI --> CAP[SAP CAP FinanceService]
  CAP --> DB[(SQLite / SAP HANA)]
  CAP --> AI[AI Agent Pipeline]
  AI --> INV[Invoice Validator]
  AI --> TAX[Tax Calculator]
  AI --> RISK[Risk Scorer]
  AI --> RPT[Report Generator]
  CAP --> BTP[SAP BTP Cloud Foundry]

docs.title: Note:
docs.text: The diagram above is a Mermaid representation for reference. For SAP Help Portal publishing, replace this code block with an exported PNG image in the images/ folder: ![Architecture diagram.](images/architecture-9a752eb.png "Finance Dashboard System Architecture")

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
The Finance Intelligence Dashboard delivers the following capabilities:

  • Real-time invoice processing status across a 7-stage pipeline with visual flow connectors
  • AI-driven validation, tax calculation, risk scoring, and automated report generation
  • Compliance score breakdown by category with progress indicators and percentage display
  • KPI cards for processed invoices, auto-calculated tax, compliance exceptions, and flagged anomalies
  • Monthly trend chart for historical invoice volume analysis with interactive bar visualization
  • Severity-based alert system with High, Medium, and Low classification and color-coded indicators
  • Invoice detail dialog with AI verdict, risk level, validation errors, and approve/reject actions
  • Fully responsive design supporting desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile viewports

For an overview of SAP Fiori dashboard design guidelines, see Dashboards .

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
The application is built on three guiding principles: transparency, automation, and responsiveness.

Transparency means every invoice carries a visible score, risk level, and AI verdict — nothing is processed silently. Finance users can drill into any invoice to see exactly what the AI assessed and why. Automation means the AI agent pipeline handles validation, tax calculation, and risk scoring without manual intervention, reducing human error and shortening cycle times. Responsiveness means the SAP Horizon theme and fluid grid layout ensure the dashboard renders correctly across device sizes, from large enterprise monitors to mobile devices.

docs.title: UI Components
docs.text:
The frontend of the Finance Intelligence Dashboard is built with SAP UI5 following the Model-View-Controller (MVC) pattern. The application is structured as a standard SAP UI5 Component with XML views, reusable XML fragments, a central controller, and a formatter utility. All UI elements conform to the SAP Horizon theme and SAP Fiori design guidelines.

The frontend lives in app/finance-dashboard/webapp/ and is served directly by the SAP CAP development server at http://localhost:4004.

docs.title: MVC Structure
docs.text:
SAP UI5 uses the MVC (Model-View-Controller) pattern to separate data, presentation, and business logic. In this application, the pattern maps to three distinct layers:

  • Models — OData V4 models configured in manifest.json bind directly to the FinanceService
  • Views — XML files in view/ define the UI structure declaratively
  • Controllers — JavaScript files in controller/ handle user interactions and data manipulation

This separation makes it easy to update the UI layout without touching business logic, and to modify controller logic without redesigning views.

For SAP Fiori presentation tier guidance, see Presentation Tier Guidance .

docs.title: XML Views
docs.text:
The application uses two XML views:

XML Views

File Purpose `App.view.xml` Root view — initializes the router and provides the application shell `Dashboard.view.xml` Main dashboard view — lays out all panels, KPI cards, pipeline, and chart

Dashboard.view.xml is the primary view. It aggregates all XML fragments into a single dashboard layout, binding each section to a specific OData entity set via named models.

docs.title: XML Fragments
docs.text:
XML fragments allow you to decompose complex views into reusable, self-contained UI blocks. Each fragment in this application maps to one dashboard panel:

XML Fragments

Fragment File Dashboard Panel Data Binding `PipelineStage.fragment.xml` 7-stage processing pipeline with status indicators `/PipelineStages` `KPICards.fragment.xml` KPI summary cards \(invoices, tax, compliance, anomalies\) `/KPIMetrics` `ComplianceScore.fragment.xml` Category compliance breakdown with progress bars `/ComplianceScores` `AlertsList.fragment.xml` Severity-based risk and anomaly alerts list `/Alerts` `AgentStatus.fragment.xml` Real-time AI agent operational status panel `/AgentStatus` `MonthlyChart.fragment.xml` Bar chart of monthly invoice volume `/MonthlyTrends` `InvoiceDetailDialog.fragment.xml` Detail dialog with AI verdict, risk level, and approve/reject actions Selected `Invoices` record

docs.title: Dashboard Controller
docs.text:
Dashboard.controller.js is the single controller for the main dashboard view. It handles:

  • Loading all OData entity sets on initialization
  • Responding to invoice row selection and opening the InvoiceDetailDialog fragment
  • Processing approve and reject actions from the detail dialog
  • Refreshing KPI and alert data after user actions

docs.title: Formatter Utility
docs.text:
utils/formatter.js provides pure data transformation functions that are called from XML view bindings. Formatters are stateless and testable in isolation. Common formatter functions in this application include:

  • Converting raw riskLevel strings to semantic color identifiers (for example, "High" → "Error")
  • Formatting decimal amounts to localized currency strings
  • Translating status codes to human-readable labels and icon sources
  • Computing progress bar values from integer compliance percentages

docs.title: Design System
docs.text:
The application uses the SAP Horizon theme with the following design tokens:

Design Tokens

Token Value Usage Primary blue `#0070F2` Primary actions, highlights, and active states Success green `#00C853` Approved invoices and passing compliance scores Warning orange `#FF9800` Medium-severity alerts and caution states Error red `#D32F2F` High-severity alerts, rejected invoices, and validation errors Background gray `#f5f6f7` Card backgrounds and panel fills

Typography uses the SAP 72 font family at 13–18px, with 600 font weight for titles and uppercase labels at 11–12px.
